items.title: The Large and Medium-sized Companies and Groups (Accounts and Reports) Regulations 2008, Schedule 7, Part 7A: energy and carbon report (unquoted companies)
items.quote: The directors’ report must state the methodologies used to calculate the information disclosed under paragraph 20D(1), (2) and (3).
items.why: The binding rule nearest to this question. Companies in scope must report emissions and energy use, state the methodology, and repeat the previous year's figures beside this year's, which only works if the data is kept. Paragraph 20D(6) allows omission where it is not practical to obtain the information, if the report says what is missing and why. Applies to unquoted companies that are not exempt: paragraph 20B(2), as shown on the page, exempts a company meeting two of three tests (turnover not more than £36 million, balance sheet total not more than £18 million, not more than 250 employees). Smaller companies are outside it.

items.title: Environmental Reporting Guidelines: including Streamlined Energy and Carbon Reporting guidance
items.publisher: HM Government (Department for Business, Energy and Industrial Strategy; Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs)
items.locator: Chapter 2, section 'Collecting your energy use data', PDF page 46; Chapter 1 principles (consistent, transparent), PDF page 9
items.quote: organisations must use verifiable data where reasonably practicable
items.why: Government's practical guidance on the data itself: meter data first, then invoices, then supplier statements; where none can be had, a reasonable estimate, showing how it was made. The principles ask for a record of all assumptions, calculations and methodologies. Dated 2019 and written for companies within the statutory regime; useful to smaller ones as a model.

items.title: UK SRS S1: General Requirements for Disclosure of Sustainability-related Financial Information
items.locator: Appendix D, paragraphs D21 to D23 (verifiability), PDF page 42; paragraph 23 (consistent data and assumptions), PDF page 10
items.quote: Information is verifiable if it is possible to corroborate either the information itself or the inputs used to derive it.
items.why: The UK's own reporting standard, based on the international standard IFRS S1. Says verifiability is helped by giving the inputs and methods of calculation and by having information reviewed and agreed by the board, and that data and assumptions must be consistent with those used in the financial statements. Paragraph 69 says the standard does not itself decide which entities must apply it.

items.title: CRR Thematic review of climate-related metrics and targets
items.locator: Section 2, cross-sector findings on data, PDF page 20
items.quote: We also encourage companies to be transparent about data limitations, including explanations of estimations and areas where it is not feasible to collect data.
items.why: Source of the quotation. The regulator's review of how listed companies report climate numbers. Notes better practice where companies gave methodologies, data assumptions and thresholds for restating earlier figures, and asks companies to be clear about the level of any assurance. About listed companies' annual reports, not smaller companies' questionnaires.

items.title: Assurance of Sustainability Reporting Market Study: Final Report
items.locator: Paragraph 18 and Figure 10, PDF page 15 (also the summary, PDF page 9); paragraphs 24 to 28 on quality
items.quote: 83% of assurance engagements for FTSE 350 companies in 2023 involved limited assurance
items.why: Source of the figure. Shows what 'assured' usually means in practice even for the largest companies: limited assurance, often over selected metrics. Also reports concerns about inconsistent quality among assurance providers. The data covers FTSE 350 companies only and was collected for the regulator by a third party from public reports.

items.title: The Greenhouse Gas Protocol: A Corporate Accounting and Reporting Standard (revised edition)
items.publisher: Greenhouse Gas Protocol (World Resources Institute and World Business Council for Sustainable Development)
items.locator: Chapter 7 'Managing Inventory Quality', PDF pages 50 to 53, including Table 4
items.quote: A quality management system provides a systematic process for preventing and correcting errors
items.why: The standard most carbon figures are built on, and its chapter on data quality. Says data quality matters more than method, asks for a person or team responsible for quality, a record of methods, data and assumptions, and routine checks such as testing a sample of input data for transcription errors. Guidance within a voluntary standard.

items.title: UK government conversion factors for company reporting of greenhouse gas emissions
items.publisher: Department for Energy Security and Net Zero
items.locator: Opening description and the list of updates to the page
items.quote: The UK government conversion factors enable users to calculate and report greenhouse gas emissions from UK operations based on activity data.
items.why: Why a refresh date matters. A new set of factors is published each year (2026 added on 11 June 2026), so a carbon figure is only reproducible if the year of the factors used is recorded. The page's update history shows a new set added each year.

items.title: PPN 006: Technical standard for completion of Carbon Reduction Plans
items.locator: Paragraphs 11 to 13 (annual review and publication) and 21 to 22 (conversion factors and boundary)
items.quote: Suppliers’ Carbon Reduction Plans should be reviewed and updated annually
items.why: A concrete case of collect once, reuse: one plan, in a set format, updated each year, published on the supplier's website and used for every bid in scope. Requires emissions to be calculated with the UK government conversion factors and in line with the GHG Protocol. Applies only to bidders for larger central government contracts.

items.title: Voluntary sustainability reporting standard for non-listed SMEs (VSME)
items.locator: Paragraph 9 (qualities of information), PDF page 6; paragraph 18 (avoiding duplication); list of disclosures B1 to B11 and C1 to C9
items.quote: The undertaking shall report information that is relevant, faithful, comparable, understandable and verifiable.
items.why: European comparator and the structure the existing briefing proposes for the dataset. Sets eleven basic disclosures and nine further ones, and lets a business refer to information already published elsewhere 'to avoid publishing the same information twice'. This is EFRAG's own text; its legal status in the EU after the 2025 to 2026 changes is covered in the briefs on value-chain reporting and was not checked here. Not UK law.
